title: Probe scenario matrix and mini-bench logbook
body:
Purpose and high-level goal:

This doc collects a compact scenario matrix, minimal microbench recipes, and a running lab log for lightweight regression triage. The aim is pragmatic: enable a small on-call or feature-owner to (1) decide whether a performance regression is real, (2) get a reproducible microbench or replay to demonstrate the impact, and (3) surface likely root causes (kernel choice, scheduler pressure, KV cache churn).

Why this lives alongside the larger harness: the main harness produces rich traces and stable CI lanes. That is necessary but slow and heavyweight. This note focuses on a fast, deterministic set of probes that let engineers iterate quickly while we run longer jobs in parallel. Think of this as the first 30–60 minute triage playbook.

Conventions and measurement rules:
- Always run 3 cold-start trials and 3 warm-start trials when measuring single-node kernels; report median and IQR.
- Use the same input seed set for generation sampling (seed file in linked_artifacts or /mnt/bench-seeds/mini-1.json).
- Wall-clock latency: measure 95th percentile across N requests per trial (N defined per scenario).
- Throughput: tokens/sec measured from runtime counters, cross-checked with token deltas in trace events.
- Cost approximation: tokens/sec * power-profile constant (on the quick path, use node-type multipliers in /infra/bench-multipliers).
- Noise budget: if measured 95p changes by < 6% across runs, mark as noise and escalate only if persistent for 24 hours or seen in CI canonical lanes.

Scenario matrix (fast probes):
- S1-small-context-single-request:
  - Inputs: single request, 128 prefix tokens, 64 generated tokens.
  - Purpose: kernel warmup, basic scheduling overhead.
  - Config: single worker, batching disabled, KV cache disabled.
  - Expected metric: baseline kernel latency.
- S2-prefix-heavy-kv-hit:
  - Inputs: 2 requests, one with long prefix (2048 tokens) then repeated short queries to exercise KV cache.
  - Purpose: validate KV caching correctness and eviction-related latency spikes.
  - Config: KV enabled, cache-size set to 2x working-set, continuous requests to check hit ratio.
- S3-batch-pressure-1-2:
  - Inputs: burst of 16 concurrent short requests (8–32 tokens).
  - Purpose: test scheduler batching decisions and kernel selection under throughput mode.
  - Config: autoscale disabled, simulate queueing by staggering 10ms arrivals.
- S4-long-context-kernel-path:
  - Inputs: single request with 8k context (where available); or synthetic long-mem trace for older arch models.
  - Purpose: force alternative kernels and confirm memory/kernel selection logic.
- S5-regression-smoke-on-fallback:
  - Inputs: 50 requests with mix of short/long; intentionally trigger fallback policy to smaller model variant (route to legacy quantized kernel).
  - Purpose: observe difference in latency profile and p99 behavior when fallback occurs.

Quick-run checklist (what to run first):
1) Sanity: run S1 and compare to the golden median from the last good run (see run-history section). If difference < 6%, stop — likely noise.
2) KV suspicion: if p95 > baseline by >15% and traces show KV cache misses >10% for repeated prefixes, run S2 with instrumentation.
3) Scheduler suspicion: if S1 looks fine but bursts show p95 jump, run S3 and capture kernel choices for each batch.
4) Fallback/variant suspicion: run S5 to validate that routing/fallback occurred and measure delta.

Minimal instrumentation to enable in quick probe runs:
- Trace: condensed mode (event types: RPC-enter, schedule, kernel-select, kernel-enter, kernel-exit, kv-lookup, kv-evict).
- Counters: per-request token counts, latency_ms, kernel_id, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio.
- Export: JSON line logs to /tmp/minibench-runs/<run-id>.jsonl and snapshot of monitoring counters to <run-id>.meta.json

Run-history (short logbook) — keep this updated as you triage:
- 2024-09-12 | run-20240912-01 | S1 | median p95=24.3ms | baseline (golden) p95=23.1ms | notes: small jitter, infra noise
- 2024-09-14 | run-20240914-03 | S3 | p95 surge to 48ms under 16-concurrency | kernel-selection: native-fused on 60% batches, fallback to slow-fp32 on some large batches | hypothesis: kernel cache TTL causing recompile/slow path
- 2024-09-27 | run-20240927-02 | S2 | observed KV hit ratio drop from 94% -> 67% over 200 requests; p95 increased 28% | action: increased cache-size and re-ran - recovered to 92% hits
- 2024-10-18 | run-20241018-01 | S5 | p99 spike when routing to model-variant-b | traced to routing rule update in RW-2147 | rollback applied and p99 back to baseline

Regression triage template (fill quickly):
- Symptom (metrics & when):
- First-run scenario used:
- Quick evidence (attach run-id and trace snapshot):
- Likely subsystem (pick one): "kernel", "scheduler", "kv-cache", "routing", "infra"
- Immediate mitigation taken:
- Next steps owner / ETA:

Golden-trace diff technique (how we compare traces fast):
1) Normalize timestamps to request-relative time (start at 0).
2) Strip non-deterministic fields (thread ids, ephemeral gradient-build ids).
3) Map kernel ids to canonical names using /infra/kernel-catalog; compare sequence of kernel-enter events per request.
4) Highlight differences: added extra kernel-enter (recompile), increased kernel-enter duration > 2x, or extra kv-evict events.

Common failure patterns we have seen (and quick checks):
- Pattern: intermittent p95 regressions correlated with spike in kernel compile events.
  - Quick check: count kernel-compile events in trace; if >0 and coincident with p95 increase -> clear.
- Pattern: long-tail spikes when KV hit ratio drops during repeated prefixes.
  - Quick check: compute per-prefix hist hit ratio by request fingerprint.
- Pattern: tiny p95 regressions on all scenarios after scheduler change.
  - Quick check: run S1 and S3; if only S3 changes, suspect batch formation heuristic or queue latency.

Open hypotheses and experiments to run next (short list):
- H1: kernel TTL eviction too aggressive for steady-state long-prefix clients. Experiment: double TTL and run S2 for 30 minutes to check hit ratio drift.
- H2: batchizer heuristic underestimates memory cost for certain model-shapes -> causes silent recompile. Experiment: synthetic workload with variance in sequence lengths and instrument kernel-select reasons.
- H3: KV cache alignment with quantization shards causes cross-shard eviction storms. Experiment: run mini-bench with shard-aware affinity turned on/off.

Automation notes (how to run a quick scenario locally):
- tools/mini-bench/bin/run-mini --scenario S2 --seed /mnt/bench-seeds/mini-1.json --trace-mode condensed --out /tmp/mini-<user>-<date>
- After run, upload artifacts to a temporary GCS bucket and add link in the run-history line.

Questions to resolve (open):
- Should we make the condensed trace mode the default for quick probes? pros: smaller, faster to analyze; cons: may drop subtle memory churn signals.
- What is the appropriate noise threshold (%) to trigger automated tickets from the quick probes? current suggestion in this doc: 6% (needs validation).

Appendix: quick filters and greps we use often:
- Count kernel-compiles: grep 'kernel-compile' *.jsonl | wc -l
- KV hit ratio per request: jq -r '.kv_hit_ratio' *.meta.json | awk '{sum += $1; count++} END {print sum/count}'
- Kernel sequence per request: jq -c '.events | map(select(.type=="kernel-enter") | .kernel_name)' /tmp/mini-*/run-*.jsonl

Last updated notes: keep this doc short. If you add a new scenario or a noteworthy run, append a single line to the run-history above and add any artifacts to linked_artifacts. If in doubt, escalate to on-call eng-serving-runtime and reference JIRA RW-2147.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (author)
